content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To make a spider man costume, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Purchase high-quality red and blue spandex fabric (3 hours)
Step 2. Research different Spider-Man suit iterations for design inspiration (2 hours)
Step 3. Create a detailed measurement chart of your body (30 minutes)
Step 4. Digitize your paper patterns into a sewing software (4 hours)
Step 5. Perform a final fit test of the completed suit (15 minutes)
Step 6. Cut the blue fabric panels for the legs and torso (1 hour)
Step 7. Wash and pre-shrink all fabric rolls (5 hours)
Step 8. Print the 3D web patterns onto the red fabric (6 hours)
Step 9. Purchase specialized fabric paint and puff additives (1 hour)
Step 10. Draft the initial paper patterns for the mask (2 hours)
Step 11. Hand-stitch the hidden zippers into the side seams (3 hours)
Step 12. Apply anti-fray sealant to all raw fabric edges (4 hours)
Step 13. Install the neck gasket for a seamless mask transition (1 hour)
Step 14. Reinforce the high-stress seams with double stitching (2 hours)
Step 15. Create the inner lining for the torso (3 hours)
Step 16. Fabricate the internal face shell for the mask shape (5 hours)
Step 17. Design the 3D-printed web shooters (4 hours)
Step 18. Order a specialized mannequin for assembly (1 week)
Step 19. Sketch the placement for the chest emblem (1 hour)
Step 20. Source durable rubber for the boot soles (2 hours)
Step 21. Take a full-body 3D scan for precision fitting (1 hour)
Step 22. Cut the eye holes into the spandex mask (20 minutes)
Step 23. Cast the back spider emblem in urethane resin (4 hours)
Step 24. Mount the back spider emblem to the suit (1 hour)
Step 25. Calibrate the industrial sewing machine (30 minutes)
Step 26. Purchase magnetic clips for the lens attachment (45 minutes)
Step 27. Print the digital patterns onto transfer paper (2 hours)
Step 28. Glue the rubber soles to the fabric boots (3 hours)
Step 29. Cut out the red fabric panels for the arms (1 hour)
Step 30. Shade the muscle groups on the fabric using an airbrush (5 hours)
Step 31. Sew the arm panels to the torso (2 hours)
Step 32. Draft the master patterns for the gloves (3 hours)
Step 33. Assemble the individual finger pieces (4 hours)
Step 34. Buy high-strength textile adhesive (30 minutes)
Step 35. Attach the finished gloves to the sleeves (1 hour)
Step 36. Pin the red and blue panels together for fit checking (2 hours)
Step 37. Stitch the main torso panels together (4 hours)
Step 38. Create a duct tape body double for sizing (3 hours)
Step 39. Sand the 3D printed components for smoothness (6 hours)
Step 40. Purchase specialized mesh for the eye lenses (30 minutes)
Step 41. Design the forearm gauntlets (3 hours)
Step 42. Watch tutorials on invisible seam techniques (2 hours)
Step 43. Install the crotch gusset for mobility (1 hour)
Step 44. Purchase a heavy-duty serger machine (2 hours)
Step 45. Sketch the back spider design (1 hour)
Step 46. Sew the mask panels together (2 hours)
Step 47. Trace the web patterns onto the fabric with chalk (3 hours)
Step 48. Buy a variety of upholstery needles (1 hour)
Step 49. Draft the pattern for the shoulder joints (2 hours)
Step 50. Coat the soles in a non-slip grip spray (2 hours)
Step 51. Install the eye lenses into the mask (1 hour)
Step 52. Purchase flexible boning for the neck structure (1 hour)
Step 53. Prime the 3D printed web shooters (2 hours)
Step 54. Assemble the lower leg sections (3 hours)
Step 55. Sew the reinforced heel cups (2 hours)
Step 56. Cut the mesh for the eye lenses (15 minutes)
Step 57. Design the utility belt clips (2 hours)
Step 58. Paint the web shooters with metallic silver (1 hour)
Step 59. Attach the boot soles to the leg panels (2 hours)
Step 60. Seal the airbrushed muscle shading with fixative (3 hours)
Step 61. Apply the raised puff paint to the web lines (8 hours)
Step 62. Order high-tensile strength thread (3 days)
Step 63. Cut the fabric for the neck and collar (1 hour)
Step 64. Build the lens frames using a 3D pen (3 hours)
Step 65. Buy fog-resistant spray for the lenses (20 minutes)
Step 66. Purchase a professional steam iron (1 hour)
Step 67. Hand-sew the chest spider emblem (4 hours)
Step 68. Measure and cut the elastic for the waist (1 hour)
Step 69. Search for reference photos of the back spider (1 hour)
Step 70. Mix the custom red fabric dye (1 hour)
Step 71. Sew the leg panels together (3 hours)
Step 72. Purchase foam padding for the shoulders (45 minutes)
Step 73. Connect the upper and lower suit halves (2 hours)
Step 74. Cut the ventilation holes in the underarms (30 minutes)
Step 75. Glue the magnetic lenses to the face shell (1 hour)
Step 76. Hem the bottom of the torso (1 hour)
Step 77. Download a 3D model for the lenses (1 hour)
Step 78. Cut the fabric for the red "boots" sections (1 hour)
Step 79. Buy white perforated vinyl for the eyes (30 minutes)
Step 80. Clear-coat the web shooters for protection (2 hours)
Step 81. Pad the interior of the mask for comfort (2 hours)
Step 82. Purchase a high-quality cutting mat and rotary cutter (1 hour)
Step 83. Print the chest emblem on vinyl (2 hours)
Step 84. Sew the invisible back zipper (3 hours)
Step 85. Cut the foam inserts for the boots (1 hour)
Step 86. Draft the pattern for the thumb gussets (1 hour)
Step 87. Transfer the pattern markings to the fabric (4 hours)
Step 88. Add hidden loops for the web shooters (1 hour)
Step 89. Steam the finished suit to remove wrinkles (45 minutes)
Step 90. Buff the eye lenses to a high shine (1 hour)
Step 91. Inventory all supplies and tools (2 hours)
Step 92. Purchase a storage garment bag (30 minutes)
Step 93. Buy specialized athletic undergarments (1 hour)
Step 94. Conduct a mobility stress test on the seams (1 hour)
Step 95. Reinforce the stitching around the wrists (1 hour)
Step 96. Apply a water-repellent spray to the fabric (2 hours)
Step 97. Pack the costume for a convention (30 minutes)
Step 98. Take professional photos of the finished costume (2 hours)
Step 99. Perform a final inspection for loose threads (1 hour)
Step 100. Mix the epoxy for the web shooter magnets (30 minutes)
